title: Interim capacity escrow and pulse-crediting workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement an interim "pulse" crediting system backed by a capacity escrow to handle short, unanticipated traffic spikes for Dedicated fleets. The goal is to allow tenants to consume short-lived extra throughput without immediate hard overage or throttling, while ensuring transparent metering and a deterministic reconciliation path for invoices. This ticket scopes the core runtime hooks, billing ledger entries, operator controls for reclaiming pulse credits, and console/ API surfaces needed for visibility and dispute resolution.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime: Requests for transient credit are satisfiable from the escrow when fleet headroom exists and are charged as 'pulse' events in metering stream.
Billing: Pulses are recorded as distinct ledger rows with timestamp, owner namespace, pulse-size (vCPU/GPU-min equivalent) and amortized window for invoice smoothing.
Operator controls: Console operators can view active pulses, manually revoke unconsumed credits, and adjust escrow pool sizing via safe rollbacks.
API/Console: Tenants see a 'pulse history' feed with usage, estimated invoice delta, and dispute button that opens a support workflow.
Telemetry: Alerts fire when escrow utilization exceeds 70% and when per-tenant pulse consumption rate exceeds configured SLA thresholds.
E2E tests: Integration tests validate credit issuance, consumption, reclaimed pulses, and reconciliation job idempotency across restart.
Docs: Design doc + console UX screenshots published and linked in the ticket.
implementation_notes: Pulse model: Implement small time-bucketed credits (e.g., 1-5 minute pulses) that decrement KV cache-aware counters in the serving runtime to avoid head-of-line stalls.
Escrow accounting: Maintain an immutable pulse ledger in Bigtable (append-only) for invoice traceability; reconciliation job computes prorated charges across a sliding 4-hour amortization window.
Rate signals: Use existing autoscaler signals but add a 'pulse-granted' metric so we can correlate granted pulses with node spin-up to avoid paying for long warmups.

Operator reclaim: Reclaim API will mark pulses as 'revoked' and emit a compensating ledger event; runtime rejects further consumption after the revocation point but allows small grace consumption to finish in-flight.
Trade-offs: Short pulses reduce billing surprise but require more ledger volume and reconciliation complexity; chosen amortization window trades immediate accuracy for invoice stability.
Privacy/safety: Pulse ledger rows contain tenant ID and usage amounts but no request payloads. KMS keys already used for billing exports apply.
Backward compatibility: Tenants without pulse-enabled plans receive existing throttling behavior; feature flag gating in runtime + console rollout planned.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): Runtime stub + unit tests behind feature flag; local ledger emulator; no billing exports. (ETA 1 week).
Phase 2 (staging): Full ledger writes, billing export consumer that writes pulses to ephemeral billing queue; console 'pulse history' read-only UI; internal alpha with 3 tenants. (ETA 2 weeks).
Phase 3 (canary): Enable for 10% of Dedicated fleets with monitoring and automatic kill-switch if escrow oversubscription > 90% for 10min. (ETA 1 week).
Phase 4 (GA): Open to eligible plans with docs, SLA language, and accounting-runbook for disputes. (ETA aligned with dedicated-2025.03 release).
telemetry_and_alerts: Metric: escrow_utilization_percentage by region and fleet. Alert at 70% warn / 90% critical.
Metric: pulses_granted_per_minute per tenant. Alert when > tenant_quota_rate for configured window.
Trace: tag traces with pulse_id to link latency regressions to pulse events.
SLO impact: Automated dashboard that shows 95th/99th tail latency pre/post pulse for sampled requests.
Reconciliation job telemetry: success rate, runtime, duplicate-detection counts.
docs_and_links: Reconciliation runner: job spec in infra repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/blob/main/jobs/pulse-reconcile.yaml
